preds: In Jordan, the press and publications law was recently amended to protect the right to express opinions on the Internet.
At the same time, journalists and free speech activists staged a peaceful protest in front of the parliament that is responsible for enforcing the law.
As leaders, activists advocating for internet freedom in Banner have called for a moment of silence in Jordan to mourn the death of the internet.
The so-called internet cemetery saw activists dress in black to protest this law.
The law in question is still in effect; it requires the signature of King Abdullah II before it can be implemented in Jordan, along with the approval of the upper parliament and all relevant laws.
Jamil Nimer, a member of parliament who opposed the law, not only resisted it but also took part in the protest..
According to them, such laws only serve to silence the voices of the people by restricting freedom.
Website owners are responsible for the comments posted on their websites, including those made by their visitors.
The controversial law has sparked strong opposition, and immediately, online activists have launched a campaign to draw attention to the uproar caused among netizens.
On Twitter, netizens expressed their frustration in writing.
